title: Keys Two and Six Swapped  (Las llaves Dos y Seis, cambiadas)

segments.t: De vuelta en la recepción, Graham apunta con su lápiz de carpintero a dos ganchos de latón vacíos en el tablero de madera, mientras Arthur se palpa la frente y Hannah llega derrapando. Escucha primero toda la escena.
Report, Graham! Which room keys went sideways during the noon telephone call?
Look at my paper book: two young hikers booked Room Two on the first floor.
Yes, lovely polite hikers — and a quiet lady with a floral hatbox booked Room Six!
Now tell Hannah where your glasses were when you handed out tags Two and Six.
Oh dear... upside down, two becomes five, no — two and six look remarkably similar blurry!
Did the hikers take backpacks to Room Six while the hatbox went to Room Two?!
Lucky for you, boss, both guests dropped their bags outside the doors and went for lunch!
Really?! Neither guest unlocked the wrong room or unpacked a single shirt yet?!
I passed them at the gate two minutes ago asking where to buy noon soup.
Graham, your eyes are worth their weight in gold — can we move the bags right now?
And leave clean welcome notes on each door table explaining the right hook number!
Grab the master ring, Hannah; you take the hatbox, and I have the two backpacks.
Ahora desmenucemos la escena del enredo de las llaves, frase por frase.
Report, Graham! Which room keys went sideways during the noon telephone call?
'¡Informe, Graham! ¿Qué llaves de habitación se descolocaron durante la llamada del mediodía?'
Look at my paper book: two young hikers booked Room Two on the first floor.
'Mira mi libro de papel: dos excursionistas jóvenes reservaron la habitación Dos en el primer piso.'
Yes, lovely polite hikers — and a quiet lady with a floral hatbox booked Room Six!
'Sí, unos excursionistas encantadores y educados, ¡y una señora tranquila con una sombrerera de flores reservó la habitación Seis!'
Now tell Hannah where your glasses were when you handed out tags Two and Six.
'Ahora dile a Hannah dónde tenías las gafas cuando repartiste las chapas Dos y Seis.'
Oh dear... upside down, two becomes five, no — two and six look remarkably similar blurry!
'Ay, Dios... al revés, el dos se convierte en cinco, no: ¡el dos y el seis se ven notablemente parecidos y borrosos!'
Did the hikers take backpacks to Room Six while the hatbox went to Room Two?!
'¿Los excursionistas llevaron las mochilas a la habitación Seis mientras la sombrerera iba a la habitación Dos?'
Lucky for you, boss, both guests dropped their bags outside the doors and went for lunch!
'¡Por suerte para ti, jefe, los dos huéspedes dejaron las bolsas fuera de las puertas y se fueron a almorzar!'
Really?! Neither guest unlocked the wrong room or unpacked a single shirt yet?!
'¿En serio? ¿¡Ninguno de los dos abrió la habitación equivocada ni sacó todavía una sola camisa!?'
I passed them at the gate two minutes ago asking where to buy noon soup.
'Me crucé con ellos en el portón hace dos minutos; preguntaban dónde comprar sopa para el mediodía.'
Graham, your eyes are worth their weight in gold — can we move the bags right now?
'Graham, tus ojos valen su peso en oro. ¿Podemos mover las bolsas ahora mismo?'
And leave clean welcome notes on each door table explaining the right hook number!
'¡Y dejar notas de bienvenida limpias en la mesita de cada puerta que expliquen el número de gancho correcto!'
Grab the master ring, Hannah; you take the hatbox, and I have the two backpacks.
'Agarra la llave maestra, Hannah; tú llevas la sombrerera y yo me encargo de las dos mochilas.'
Escuchemos la conversación entera una vez más.

Lucky for you, boss, both guests dropped their bags outside the doors and went for lunch!
Really?! Neither guest unlocked the wrong room or unpacked a single shirt yet?!
I passed them at the gate two minutes ago asking where to buy noon soup.
Graham, your eyes are worth their weight in gold — can we move the bags right now?
And leave clean welcome notes on each door table explaining the right hook number!
Grab the master ring, Hannah; you take the hatbox, and I have the two backpacks.
Gracias a la sopa del almuerzo en la calle Linden, Hannah y Graham tienen quince minutos para dejar cada bolsa en la puerta correcta. Nos vemos arriba en la próxima escena.
See you next time!
